Notation

Write music down in whatever order suits you: chords, a rhythm, the notes, the words, in any order. Work in chunks and enter each chunk its own way. Click a note on the staff and move it with the arrow keys.

Start here

The piece
Tonality

Voices

Chunks

j / k select the next / previous chunk; Alt+j / k move it down / up; Shift+Alt+j / k move its section. Top to bottom is start to end. What you enter goes into the selected row. Sections (Verse, Chorus ...) gather the chunks under them, fold like headings, and move or duplicate as a block. Style opens the Backing Track on its Band tab for that row: what you set there is kept here, for the chunk, the section, or (with the button in The piece) the whole piece. The most particular wins: a chunk's own settings, else its section's, else the piece's.

Chords

| between bars. Two chords in a bar split it in half, three in thirds.

Rhythm

A rhythm needs a meter. Choose one first:

Notes

Waiting for a rhythm

Words

One syllable for each note of the first voice. Put a hyphen between the syllables of a word.

Play it in time

Listens to a MIDI keyboard and to the computer keys (laid out as a piano). What you play replaces this chunk's notes (and rhythm), or its chords, in the voice chosen above.

The music
Nothing selected

Shift+click a second note to select everything between (one voice), then copy (Ctrl/⌘+C), cut (X), paste after it (V) or Delete. Click a note, then ↑ ↓ move it to the next note in the key, Shift+↑ ↓ by a half step, Alt+↑ ↓ by an octave. ← → pick the note before or after, Esc lets go. Slashes are rhythm with no note yet.

DWIM

Do what I mean: select bars that were played in (Play it in time) and press DWIM to see the other ways they could be written, best first. The playing is kept with the chunk, so this keeps working after edits elsewhere, after splitting on a bar line, merging, duplicating, and after a reload.

ABC

Edit the code and the staff follows. Chunks start at "^Name" labels and at [M:] / [K:] changes; voices are [V:1] lines.

ChordPro

The chords and words of the piece. ChordPro has no rhythm or notes: reading it in replaces the piece with its chords (one a bar, or as the | marks say) and words.
